implementation.name: original-v2-comm-compute-overlap
implementation.scope: The original four-layer backward order L4 → L1. One gradient transfer per illustrated layer, in the same collective order on all ranks. Timeline widths and motion are schematic, not a performance model; o occupies the GPU before launch.
implementation.question: When is a gradient ready for communication and for the optimizer?

purpose: When is a gradient ready for communication and for the optimizer?
storyboard: The GPU is computing L4 gradients. No gradient can be communicated before its backward work completes.
Local g4 is complete. The GPU must pay nonoverlappable overhead o4 before its AllReduce launches.
After o4, g4 is in flight on the network while the GPU computes L3. g4 is not yet safe for the optimizer.
AllReduce L4 has completed within the later backward window. The GPU now holds reduced Σg4 and local g3; o3 precedes its launch.
g3 communicates while the GPU computes L2. The earlier reduced gradient remains live for the later optimizer step.
Σg3 joins Σg4. Local g2 is ready, and o2 still occupies the GPU before the next transfer.
g2 communicates while the GPU computes L1. The same layer cannot hide its own gradient transfer because that gradient was unavailable before backward finished.
All backward work is complete. Local g1 is ready, but o1 and its AllReduce have no remaining backward computation to hide behind.
After o1, g1 communicates while the GPU waits. The optimizer cannot consume local g1 as though it were globally reduced.
Σg1 has arrived. All four required reduced gradients are now available, so the optimizer dependency is satisfied.

The optimizer consumes the completed reduced gradients and updates the parameters. Earlier overlap hid communication only within the illustrated later-compute windows; the final tail remained exposed.
guard: AllReduce launches only after gradient readiness and GPU overhead, in fixed L4-to-L1 order. Optimizer waits for all reductions. Hiding a transfer depends on later compute and completion timing; no claim that every real workload hides all but the last bucket.
